concrete.name: Concreters and paving
concrete.desc: Driveways, slabs, foundations, polished and exposed aggregate floors, paving and kerbing
profile: Share of work that is residential (%)
Geotechnical report, engineer's design or council inspection required for slabs?
Cutting, drilling or excavating near services, reinforcing or post-tension cables?
Ready-mix supplier and concrete testing records kept?

gen: Concrete pumps, mixers, saws, screeds and trailers. Values, theft from sites and vehicles, and hired-in plant.
liab: Cracked or uneven slabs, poor falls, scaling and discoloured finishes are the usual disputes. Ask about subgrade preparation, reinforcing, curing, weather conditions and who signs off the work. These are defective workmanship exposures, so ask for the extension.
Cutting or drilling through electrical, gas, water or post-tension cables. Ask about scanning before coring and records of services located.
Excavation for footings and vibration or washout near boundaries. Check removal of support and adjoining property exclusions.
Pump boom contact with powerlines, hose failures and trucks damaging driveways and kerbs. Check whether the policy covers plant used for hire work.
mdamage: Check theft of saws, screeds and small plant from vehicles and sites, and the basis of valuation.

buildwash.name: Building, roof and exterior washing
buildwash.desc: Soft washing, water blasting, roof and house washing, moss and mould treatment, graffiti and gutter cleaning
profile: Roof work on tile, long-run steel, membrane or coated roofs?
Chemicals used such as bleach, sodium hypochlorite or biocides?
Run-off captured, filtered or diverted from drains and waterways?
Maximum water pressure used (PSI or bar)
Work near powerlines, solar panels or electrical fittings?
Rope access, EWPs or ladders used for high work?

gen: Washing units, pumps, trailers and vehicles. Values, theft, and fire or breakdown of mounted plant.
liab: Damage to what is being washed

Water forced behind cladding, stripped paint or coatings, etched glass, damaged seals, cracked tiles and roof damage are the main claims. This is exactly the PBWO exposure that most liability policies exclude, so ask for the PBWO extension and check the limit.
Bleach and biocides can damage plants, paving, metal and finishes, and discolour surfaces. Ask about chemical choice, dilution, plant protection and rinsing.
High pressure water entering walls, roof spaces and electrical fittings. Ask about pressure limits, cladding and window seal checks, and wet surfaces creating slip hazards for others.
Roof and wall washing from ladders, roofs and EWPs. Check safe-work methods, edge protection and any exclusion for work above a stated height.
Wash water, chemicals and moss debris entering stormwater. Check the pollution exclusion and any council or regional rules.
mdamage: Theft of washing units and pumps from vehicles and trailers, and storage of chemicals.
